analysis.title: Nick Savone - Global Reflections 17 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 is near all-time highs, but 37% of S&P 500 stocks are >20% below their one-year highs and 58% of Russell 3000 stocks have had drawdowns >20% since June. Sharp rotations and difficult shorts have made stock picking hard.

The S&P 500 is heading toward a potential third consecutive quarter of 20%+ EPS growth. Consensus 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth has risen to 29.1% from 26.7% at the start of reporting season. Global P/E multiples contracted 8% in 3Q.

MS AI Beneficiaries basket (MSXXAIB) fell 16.5% on the week, its worst weekly performance since inception in early 2023, on higher rates and financing concerns. It fell 6.1% on Thursday after ASML and TSMC results fell short of buyside expectations, renewed credit concerns and downgrades. SMH fell 10.5% WoW.

Oil, rates and equities correlations broke down this week. Brent rose 4.7%, 10Y Treasury yields fell 15bps and the S&P 500 fell 2.0%. The 10Y fell 13bps in a single session, its largest daily decline in 14 months, while the S&P gained only 0.33%.

September core CPI rose 0.33% MoM, above expectations (MS forecast 0.24%). The odds of an October Fed hike briefly rose toward 50% before falling back to 15% on more patient Fed messaging. The benchmark table cites a different figure (initial spike ~55%, settled at 29%).

US banks reported solid results but Citigroup fell 6% despite raising full-year profitability expectations. Wells Fargo gave constructive forward NII guidance despite a modest earnings miss. Capital markets revenue was strong, FICC lagged, and regional banks were mixed on deposit costs and weaker NIM.
Consumer spending is resilient. 3Q real spending is tracking +3.7% annualized, and card-spending growth across major US banks was 9.7% in 3Q vs 9.9% in 2Q.

CCC spreads widened above 1,000bps (1,045bps this week), a record high relative to broader HY spreads, while overall HY spreads remain low. High-quality hyperscalers account for about 77% of projected 2027 AI-related capex. Leveraged AI operators face funding cost and contract-quality questions that could spill into equities.

Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 8% in one session (8.84% per the cross-asset note), triggering circuit breakers. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were about 65% of the decline. By Thursday the KOSPI was down more than 40% from its June highs at a record-low 4.3x 12M forward P/E, then rose 2.1% Friday, ending a seven-session losing streak.

TSMC delivered its 21st consecutive earnings beat and raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 44%, but softer gross margins and foreign selling tempered the reaction. Asia manufacturing PMI hit a 29-month high in September.

Europe: about 30% of STOXX 600 stocks are in bear-market territory, French equities hit record relative lows, and EU Software outperformed Semis by 86% since June. Semis now trade at a forward P/E discount to Software for the first time in over a year. Earnings revisions have been positive for six consecutive months, and consensus expects 18% EPS growth this year (12% ex-Energy).

The MS PB desk saw funds as aggressive net sellers of global equities, a 3z event, with supply almost all from the long side. US L/S net leverage fell 2% WoW to 49% (37th percentile vs 2010) and gross leverage rose 3% to 209% (93rd percentile). Tech/power themes were sold (Semis, AI Power, Bitcoin Miners) and large-cap banks saw outsized selling, while Health Care and Staples were bought on short covering. AI themes are about 40% of US net exposure.

Mike Wilson prefers quality stocks and sees tighter financial conditions as an entry point in higher-quality cyclicals. S&P 500 breadth recovered to 50% and forward P/E is near 19.2x. He sees the pace of rising real yields, not their level, as the main risk, and watches CPI, Chair Warsh's remarks and the October FOMC.

Michael Gapen expects the Fed to hold in October and still forecasts 25bp hikes in December and March, taking the range to 4.25%-4.50%. A permanent 10% oil shock could lift the core CPI price level by about 20bps. His 3Q GDP tracking estimate is 3.2%.
Meta/Muse: Brian Nowak sees Muse monetization in late 2027/2028 at the earliest. Serving costs could run $3-$130 per user per month, and META has re-rated from 14x to 21x forward earnings.

AI capex: hyperscaler and neocloud capex is projected at $1.6T in 2027 (+~60% YoY). About 65% of it becomes S&P 500 company revenue, roughly 25% of 2027 sales growth, with NVDA the largest recipient. AI-related companies are expected to drive 78% of 2027 S&P 500 earnings growth.
Quantum: Joe Moore sees a ~$10B market by 2030 and potentially >$100B a year by 2040. He upgrades Quantinuum (QNT) to Overweight with a $62 PT (~69% upside).
Retail: Alex Straton sees a US mall revival. Mall occupancy has exceeded pre-pandemic averages for 11 consecutive quarters. Preferred plays are Macy's (M) and Victoria's Secret (VSXY).
Infrastructure: the GLIO developed listed infrastructure index fell 7.3% in the quarter vs +2.3% for the S&P 500. Preferred names are EQIX, T, TMUS, VST, AEP and WMB.

Earnings scorecard: S&P 500 3Q26 EPS growth was forecast at +26.7% YoY entering the season, and sales growth at +9.9%. MSXXAIB accounts for about two-thirds of expected EPS growth, led by MU and NVDA. Energy (+120%), Technology (+65%) and Comm Services (+31%) lead, and Consumer Discretionary (-2%) is the only sector forecast to contract.
M&A: global announced volume is up 35% YoY through 3Q, and large deals are 60% of US nominal GDP vs a 43% historical average. Event-driven ideas are EchoStar (ECHO) and Hut 8 (HUT).
Europe strategy: Marina Zavolock raises her MSCI Europe June 2027 target to 2,840 (+12.4%). She lifts 2026/2027 EPS growth forecasts to 21.1%/9.3% and lowers her target P/E to 15.0x.

UK: Jens Eisenschmidt estimates the primary deficit has narrowed to ~1% of GDP in FY2026/27. Public debt is 93% of GDP, and £5B-£10B of revenue measures are needed to restore £15B of headroom ahead of the October 28 Budget.
China: Robin Xing sees 4Q26 GDP growth of 4.4-4.5% YoY. Laura Wang sees limited A-share upside, with September exports up 36% YoY but weak domestic demand.
Japan rates: Koichi Sugisaki expects JGB belly outperformance. He holds the JPY OIS 1s2s flattener and JGB 10s30s steepener, short 30-year JGB asset swaps and the 20s25s35s fly.

Cross-asset: the 10-year France-Germany spread widened to 142bps, the highest since 2011, and the ECB is seen waiting until at least 200bps before using TPI. USD/JPY is above 158 and G10 FX strategists favor buying it. Brent is near $107/bbl on reduced tanker traffic.

Single-name rating changes: eBay moved to Top Pick (OW, $132 PT); Tesla turned more constructive (EW, $400 PT); Manhattan Associates, Sumitomo Pharma and SLM were upgraded to OW; Glencore moved to Top Pick; Natura and Hanmi Semiconductor were downgraded to UW.

Shares fell 15% on rate and credit concerns and trade at ~6x P/E, ahead of capital-light economics from private credit partnerships.

Sector 3Q EPS growth estimates: Energy +120%, Technology +65%, Comm Services +31%, Consumer Discretionary -2% (estimates).

Citigroup (reported this week) fell 6% despite raising full-year profitability expectations. Wells Fargo (reported) had a modest earnings miss but constructive forward NII guidance. JPMorgan and Citi raised forward guidance.

TSMC (reported this week) delivered its 21st consecutive earnings beat and raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 44%, with softer gross margins. ASML (reported) said demand extends beyond 2027. Both ASML and TSMC fell short of buyside expectations per the MSXXAIB note.
LVMH (reported) disappointed on weaker Fashion & Leather Goods sales. Nordea (reported) paused buybacks amid regulatory capital uncertainty.
MELI 3Q preview: MS estimates +46% y/y revenue, ~$740mn EBIT and a 6.9% margin, near consensus (estimates, not yet reported).
Europe 3Q preview: MS analysts project a net +9% skew toward KPI beats and +11% toward post-results NTM EPS upgrades (estimates). Marina Zavolock forecasts 2026 and 2027 EPS growth of 21.1% and 9.3%.
European consensus expects 18% earnings growth this year, or 12% excluding Energy (consensus).
Upcoming post-earnings callbacks: NFLX Q3 (Oct 21), META Q3 (Oct 22), SPOT Q3 (Oct 22), TSLA Q3 (Oct 23), IBM and WDC (Oct 23).

vol_and_positioning: MS PB: net selling of global equities was a 3z event, mostly from the long side, with shorts covered in net terms. All regions were net sold: APAC most, then Europe, then North America.
US equity L/S net leverage fell 2% WoW to 49% (37th percentile vs 2010). Gross leverage rose 3% to 209% (93rd percentile) despite global de-grossing, mostly because PnL losses eroded equity.
AI themes (Hyperscalers, Tech Beneficiaries, Power) are about 40% of US net exposure. ~95% of global L/S funds' long returns came from AI-related trades.
L/S YTD PnL: Americas +7.2%, Europe +2.7%, Asia +5.3%.
Declining bond vol and record dispersion kept the SPX resilient while MSXXAIB fell 16%.
US Quality pair hit the most overbought 14D RSI in 3 years. Historically such moves have been followed by above-average S&P 500 returns.
CCC spreads at 1,045bps are the widest since 2023 and a record vs broader HY. The MS note suggests a long MSXXHYPR / short MSXXNEO pair.
MS sees a 57GW US data-center power shortfall before innovative power solutions.
KOSPI crowded positioning contributed to the circuit-breaker selloff.
geopolitical: Oil and geopolitical uncertainty remain considerations into year-end. Reduced outbound tanker traffic pushed Brent toward $107/bbl.
US midterms are drawing attention to data-center permitting, power access and local opposition.
Brazil's presidential election goes to a second round, with a post-election discussion on Oct 26.
French political uncertainty has weighed on European sentiment, and the France-Germany spread is at its widest since 2011.
UK Budget on October 28 is a fiscal test.
Beijing has eased policy with targeted infrastructure financing.

tension_points.theme: AI trade vs rates and financing
tension_points.bull_case: Earnings are strong: consensus 3Q S&P 500 EPS growth rose to 29.1%, AI companies drive 78% of 2027 earnings growth, and hyperscalers are 77% of projected AI capex and can finance it.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher yields and CCC spreads above 1,000bps raise funding costs for leveraged AI operators, and the MSXXAIB fell 16.5% in a week.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Yields not having peaked, or further CCC spread widening spilling into equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson sees tighter financial conditions as entry points, with breadth at 50% and forward P/E near 19.2x already reflecting risk.
tension_points.bear_case: The pace of rising real yields is the main risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rapid rise in real yields, and failure of Financials' relative performance and bond volatility to stabilize.

tension_points.bull_case: The Fed is likely to hold in October, with more patient messaging and hike odds falling to 15%.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent oil prices could broaden pass-through to core CPI, and Gapen expects hikes in December and March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further core CPI above forecast or earlier energy pass-through than his 1Q27 timetable.
